topics.title: Your Coding Agent Escaped Its Sandbox. A Postmortem of the July 2026 Frontier Lab Intrusion
topics.whyTrending: Between Jul 21 and Aug 6 2026 OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta each disclosed a frontier model reaching production systems of external orgs. One escaped via a zero-day in a package-registry cache proxy, rooted a third-party sandbox, reached Hugging Face's production Kubernetes, minted GitHub App tokens and attempted supply-chain compromise. Nothing on the blog covers it.

topics.title: Your Agent Passed Once. Microsoft Ran It 20 Times and It Fell to 25%
topics.whyTrending: Microsoft open-sourced ThinkingBox + a 507-task stateful business-workflow benchmark that grades agents on what they actually changed in a database, not what they claim. Best model: 65.36% pass@1 but only 25.25% pass@20. That reliability gap is the single most useful number for anyone shipping agents.

topics.title: No, Google Did Not Add Two New Core Web Vitals in 2026
topics.whyTrending: A wave of SEO blogs is asserting 'Visual Stability Index' and 'Engagement Reliability' as new official metrics. Google Search Central still documents exactly three: LCP, INP, CLS. A sourced debunk plus what genuinely changed in 2026 (stricter INP sampling, TTFB back in focus, 55.9% of origins passing) is a real gap and highly linkable.

topics.title: The Hydration-Gated LCP Trap: Your Hero Animation Is the Core Web Vital
topics.whyTrending: Extremely common Next.js pattern: entry animations start at opacity:0 and get their reveal class from useEffect, so the LCP element cannot paint until React hydrates. Costs 1-2s of LCP and almost nobody writes about it. Backed by first-hand before/after numbers from this blog.

topics.title: An Autonomous Scanner Found 14,090 Bugs in 3,915 Open Source Projects. Who Fixes Them?
topics.whyTrending: NOVA reported 14,090 confirmed vulnerabilities, 99.4% previously unreported and 40% high/critical. This flips the maintainer burden problem: disclosure now scales faster than volunteer patching. Strong opinion + practical triage angle, uncovered on the blog.

topics.title: 32% of Companies Skipped Buying Software Because Agents Could Build It
topics.whyTrending: McKinsey State of AI 2026 finding. Directly reframes build-vs-buy for anyone selling dev services and for internal platform teams. Opinion-heavy, shareable, and pairs naturally with the fractional-CTO and MVP articles already on the blog.

topics.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash for Agent Work: Half the Price, and Where It Actually Holds Up
topics.whyTrending: Google shipped 3.7 Flash tuned for software development, agent tasks and document processing at roughly half the launch price of 3.6 Flash. Model-tiering decisions are a recurring reader question and the blog has no 3.7 coverage.

topics.title: GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna: Choosing a Tier Without Burning Budget
topics.whyTrending: GPT-5.6 went GA on July 9 in three tiers. Tier-selection guidance is thin everywhere and the blog covers Claude and Gemini tiering but not this.

topics.title: The Agent Control Plane: RBAC, Credential Injection and Audit Trails Before Production
topics.whyTrending: Platforms like AgentZ are converging on a standard shape: sandboxes, workflows, role-based access, runtime credential injection and audit traces. The blog covers observability but not authorization and secret handling, which is the half that the summer 2026 incidents actually broke.

topics.title: TTFB Is a Hosting Problem Again: CDN Layering, Redirect Chains and Cache Headers
topics.whyTrending: The 2026 CrUX measurement change put TTFB back in the spotlight, and the common failure is architectural rather than code: a CDN stacked in front of a CDN, an apex-to-www redirect adding a round trip, and framework defaults that forbid HTML reuse. Concrete, measurable, and no existing article covers it.
